name: SigMF Raw-IQ Capture Source Nodes
description: Public raw-IQ archives -> SDS $IQC pointer records. Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a cron timer tick into ONE bulk hostcap/http-request GET of the configured archive's metadata index (default IQEngine: https://www.iqengine.org/api/datasources/local/local/meta, anonymous, no token, ~31 MB, 36,636 SigMF documents) plus the parser attribution job naming the source adapter; `parse` joins that job with the response, decodes each SigMF document and emits a size-prefixed $IQC record stream for hostcap/storage-ingest. $IQC IS A POINTER RECORD: it carries where the samples are (PAYLOADS[].URL), what they hash to (BYTE_SHA512 from SigMF core:sha512) and nothing else — CUSTODY stays UPSTREAM_ONLY and no payload is ever mirrored. SigMF publishes HERTZ, so SAMPLE_RATE_HZ / CENTER_FREQ_HZ / FREQ_*_EDGE_HZ carry the value unconverted ($RFB's MHz convention is deliberately NOT adopted) and DATATYPE is the SigMF token verbatim. GEOLOCATION is omitted entirely when the source published no position, and a transposed lat/lon is refused rather than swapped. LICENCE IS PER RECORDING: core:license rides verbatim and an absent one means UNKNOWN TERMS, never public domain. The source-adapter registry ships exactly one adapter, the one whose anonymous read surface was verified live; a stub adapter that fabricates data is forbidden and an unknown adapter id fails closed. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the parse method emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are pure single-pass transforms over one fetched JSON document: `request` formats a fetch descriptor from node CONFIG, and `parse` walks the archive's capture documents once, emitting one $IQC record per document into a single append-only stream. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out and nothing for a second thread to do; the whole cost is one linear scan of the metadata index. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles on the single-thread STANDALONE_WASM lane rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Builds the archive bulk-metadata fetch request + parse job from a timer tick. ONE bulk request per cycle — the per-file metadata route exists but walking it would be a 36,636-request crawl of a community-run service. The job frame names the source adapter; an adapter id absent from the registry fails closed. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

wildcardJustification.detail: Cron timer tick frame produced by the flow runtime and consumed inside this flow only; it carries no payload at all, so there is no SDS record to name.

methods.description: Decodes each SigMF document in the archive metadata index into an $IQC pointer record (Hz unconverted, DATATYPE verbatim, SEGMENTS/ANNOTATIONS/EXTENSIONS carried, GEOLOCATION omitted when unpublished or out of WGS-84 range, licence per recording, PAYLOADS pointing upstream with CUSTODY UPSTREAM_ONLY) plus the storage.ingest_with_source meta and the raw payload for archiving. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted: the host presents the ETag / Last-Modified it recorded from the last 2xx for this URL, so an unchanged document answers 304 with no body. The method then emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced. Same contract as data-source/celestrak-parser.

wildcardJustification.detail: The verbatim archive metadata index as fetched (IQEngine's SigMF document array), archived byte-for-byte for provenance. It is an external wire format with no SDS identity.

HTTP 304 notice {status:304,unchanged:true,source_name,source_url,dataset_id} produced when the origin confirms the previously fetched archive metadata index is current; an intra-flow control frame, never persisted as a record.

outputPorts.description: Emitted ONLY when the fetch answered HTTP 304 Not Modified (the host sent the recorded ETag / Last-Modified validators): one notice frame and no meta/records/raw frames, so the ingest node never becomes ready and nothing is stored or announced.
